records.title: Crude oil exports to Canada

records.limitation: National bilateral energy measure; currencies, barrel volumes and gas volumes are separate units. Rounded narrative descriptions of near-zero LNG flows are not substituted for the detailed positive series.

records.title: Canadian ultimate-owner direct investment position in the U.S.
records.summary: Inward direct investment, classified by ultimate beneficial owner.
records.limitation: Historical-cost stock classification. Foreign-parent and ultimate-owner measures must not be added. Changes in position do not establish newly completed factories or jobs; not comparable to Canada’s CAD-valued ultimate-investor series without reconciliation.

records.title: Increase in the Canadian-parent inward investment position
records.summary: Change in an accumulated position during 2025; not a transaction or completed-capex total.
records.limitation: Historical-cost stock classification. Foreign-parent and ultimate-owner measures must not be added. Changes in position do not establish newly completed factories or jobs; not comparable to Canada’s CAD-valued ultimate-investor series without reconciliation.

records.title: Initial Section 301 tariff action
records.summary: Additional 25% duties began on the first approximately USD34 billion list of Chinese goods.
records.limitation: Historical starting action, not a statement of the combined tariff now applying to every product.

records.title: Huawei Entity List licensing requirements
records.summary: The Entity List action imposed licensing requirements for covered transactions involving listed Huawei entities.
records.limitation: Entity-, item- and transaction-specific; not a ban on all U.S.–China technology trade.

records.title: Phase One agriculture and financial-services commitments
records.summary: The agreement covers intellectual property, technology transfer, agriculture, financial services and trade commitments; it entered into effect February 14, 2020.
records.limitation: A signed commitment is not proof that purchases or every market-access obligation were fulfilled.

records.title: USMCA entry into force
records.summary: The U.S., Canada and Mexico replaced NAFTA with USMCA.
records.limitation: Preferential treatment depends on coverage and origin rules; other duties can still apply.

records.title: USMCA vehicle regional value content
records.unit: % regional value content for light vehicles/core parts
records.summary: Light vehicles and core parts have a 75% regional-value-content requirement under the automotive rules.
records.limitation: Rules for core, principal and complementary parts differ; this is an eligibility rule, not a measured production gain.

records.title: USMCA high-wage content
records.summary: Passenger vehicles require 40% high-wage content; the rule is 45% for light and heavy trucks, with a USD16/hour threshold.
records.limitation: These are rule thresholds, not observed wages across all assembly jobs.

records.title: Modelled U.S. automotive employment effect of USMCA rules
records.summary: USITC estimates an automotive employment difference under its modelling assumptions.
records.limitation: Model result relative to a counterfactual; not an observed count of new 2026 jobs, not Canada-specific employment and not an effect of the September 2026 arrangements.

records.title: Modelled U.S. vehicle/parts production revenue effect
records.summary: USITC models an increase in U.S. vehicle and parts production revenue associated with the rules.
records.limitation: Revenue is not value added, net welfare or a 2026 realized investment amount.

records.title: Listed Chinese military-industrial securities restrictions
records.summary: OFAC describes prohibitions on U.S.-person purchases or sales of securities linked to designated Chinese military-industrial entities.
records.limitation: List-based securities restrictions are distinct from FDI screening and the outbound investment program; current entities and exemptions require checking the live list.

records.title: Forced-labour import presumption
records.summary: UFLPA creates a rebuttable import prohibition for covered Xinjiang-linked goods and listed entities.
records.limitation: The presumption and exception standard are supply-chain specific; a detention is not automatically a final denial or a total ban on Chinese goods.

records.title: Advanced-computing and semiconductor controls
records.summary: BIS introduced phased controls on advanced computing, semiconductor manufacturing and certain U.S.-person activities.
records.limitation: Later rules alter product thresholds and licensing. The 2022 action cannot alone describe the current treatment of every chip.

records.title: Section 301 EV tariff modification
records.unit: % additional Section 301 duty on covered EV lines
records.summary: The modification imposed an additional 100% Section 301 rate on covered Chinese EV tariff lines.
records.limitation: Product-specific additional rate. It is not the total landed tariff after other applicable duties, and it does not establish consumer savings or employment effects.

records.title: Section 301 EV-battery tariff modification
records.unit: % additional duty on covered EV-battery lines
records.summary: Covered lithium-ion EV batteries moved to a 25% Section 301 rate; non-EV batteries had a separate 2026 schedule.
records.limitation: EV and non-EV batteries have different effective dates and coverage; check the current tariff line and exclusions.

records.title: Section 301 semiconductor tariff modification
records.unit: % additional duty on covered semiconductor lines
records.summary: Covered semiconductor tariff lines moved to a 50% additional rate.
records.limitation: Tariff coverage differs from export-control licensing and can be affected by later actions.

records.title: Connected vehicle restrictions: phased requirements
records.summary: The final rule took effect March 17, 2025. Covered software/manufacturer restrictions begin with model year 2027 and hardware restrictions with model year 2030 or January 1, 2029 for non-model-year components.
records.limitation: Rule effectiveness and future model-year compliance dates are separate. The rule includes specific and general authorizations; not every restriction started in 2025.

records.title: USMCA digital trade rules
records.summary: The digital chapter covers electronic products, cross-border information flows and limits on localization.
records.limitation: Treaty text has scope conditions and public-policy/security exceptions; it is not a dollar measure of digital exports.

records.title: USMCA financial-services provisions
records.summary: Financial-services commitments address market access, transparency and data access for supervision.
records.limitation: These are legal commitments rather than observed financial-sector revenues or Canadian/U.S. jobs.

records.title: Outbound investment program in force
records.summary: Certain U.S.-person investments connected to China, Hong Kong and Macau are prohibited or notifiable in defined semiconductor, quantum and AI activities.
records.limitation: This is not a prohibition on every investment in China. The October 2026 proposal is separate from this in-force rule.

records.title: COINS outbound investment proposal
records.summary: Treasury proposed updated regulations including expanded technology coverage and invites comments before final regulations.
records.limitation: Proposal as of the review date; no final effective date or completed investment effect is established here.

records.title: Outbound investment notification enforcement
records.summary: Treasury disclosed a USD200,000 penalty issued in July 2026 for failure to notify a covered investment in a Chinese embodied-AI company.
records.limitation: A penalty is an enforcement observation, not the value of the investment or an estimate of blocked capital.

records.title: Canada’s excepted-foreign-state status
records.summary: Canada is listed as an excepted foreign state for specified CFIUS provisions, subject to investor criteria.
records.limitation: Foreign-control transactions can remain within CFIUS jurisdiction. Excepted status does not automatically clear every Canadian transaction.

records.title: Case-by-case licensing for selected AI chips
records.summary: BIS announced case-by-case review for H200, MI325X and similar chips subject to stated security conditions.
records.limitation: Licensing policy is not proof of approvals or physical shipments. Current technical scope must be read with the final rule.

records.title: Binational aerospace and maritime warning
records.summary: NORAD integrates U.S. and Canadian aerospace warning/control and maritime warning.
records.limitation: Longstanding institutional context, not a command created in 2026 and not a measure of trade, defence contracts or employment.

records.title: U.S.–China counternarcotics working group launched
records.summary: The working group provides policy and law-enforcement coordination against illicit synthetic drugs and precursor supply.
records.limitation: Bilateral coordination does not establish reductions in deaths or trafficking volumes attributable to the group.

records.title: Precursor scheduling cooperation reported
records.summary: The State Department described China’s announcement to schedule three essential fentanyl precursors after working-group discussions.
records.limitation: Report of a policy development; it does not quantify enforcement effectiveness or make all Chinese chemical exports illicit.

records.title: Joint critical-infrastructure cybersecurity advisory
records.summary: U.S. agencies and international partners, including Canada, published an advisory on PRC-sponsored Volt Typhoon activity.
records.limitation: An attributed threat assessment is not a quantified loss of trade, an employment estimate or a claim about every Chinese firm.

records.title: 30-for-30 Board of Trade recommendations
records.unit: USD billion of referenced product scope, each direction
records.summary: The two sides identified approximately USD30 billion of products in each direction for possible reciprocal tariff improvements, using a historical trade basis.
records.limitation: A scope/value reference, not USD30 billion of new sales, implemented zero duties or realized incremental exports. Domestic legal implementation and later trade data must be checked.

records.title: Canadian product coverage under Section 338
records.unit: % additional duty on specified Canadian products
records.summary: The proclamation changed which Canadian products face an additional 50% duty, effective October 30; origin under USMCA does not by itself remove the covered duty.
records.limitation: Applies to specified tariff lines, not all Canadian goods. The tariff register and other duties determine a shipment’s total treatment.

records.title: USMCA non-extension and 2027 annual review
records.summary: The Federal Register says the U.S. did not agree to extend the term at the July 1, 2026 review; annual reviews follow under the agreement.
records.limitation: Non-extension at that meeting is not immediate termination; the source identifies the existing 2036 term and extension mechanism.

records.title: U.S.–Canada opioid action-plan cooperation
records.summary: The two governments established working groups across law enforcement, border security and health under the Joint Action Plan on Opioids.
records.limitation: Coordination and meeting evidence does not quantify reduced trafficking or deaths and does not establish a trade or employment gain.

records.title: North American drug dialogue in Ottawa
records.summary: The United States, Canada and Mexico met in Ottawa on January 27–28, 2026 to coordinate responses to fentanyl and other illicit drugs.
records.limitation: Coordination and meeting evidence does not quantify reduced trafficking or deaths and does not establish a trade or employment gain.

records.title: Fentanyl seizures in the U.S. Northern Border region
records.summary: Canada’s official dashboard reports this U.S. CBP seizure mass for the Northern Border region.
records.limitation: Canadian government report citing CBP; not independently reconciled to a downloaded CBP table in this release. A border seizure region is not country of drug manufacture, total trafficking volume or causal evidence of a bilateral policy’s effectiveness. These are enforcement statistics, not merchandise imports.

records.summary: Investment income, without current-cost adjustment. BEA detailed-country workbook: xl/worksheets/sheet3.xml, cell G199.
records.limitation: Immediate counterpart / foreign-parent country classification; excludes Hong Kong as a separate counterpart. This all-industry investment measure is not financial-services-only, completed factory capex, gross merchandise trade or a job count. Position changes, transaction flows and income cannot be substituted for one another.

assessments.name: Vehicles, EVs and batteries
assessments.summary: Regional production rules coexist with restrictive treatment of covered Chinese vehicles.

questions.title: What is the connection?
questions.text: Canada participates in North American vehicle supply chains under USMCA. China-facing measures include Section 301 duties, connected-vehicle restrictions and supply-chain controls.

questions.title: Why does it matter to the United States?
questions.text: U.S. producers depend on cross-border inputs while policymakers pursue domestic production and security objectives. Price and sourcing effects can move in different directions.

questions.title: What does the evidence establish?
questions.text: The record establishes tariff/eligibility thresholds and a USITC model of automotive effects. The 5,085-job figure is modelled, rather than a new 2026 payroll count.

questions.title: What remains uncertain?
questions.text: This review does not establish a net U.S. jobs or consumer-welfare effect of the 2026 arrangements. A rule’s legal effective date can precede its model-year compliance date.

assessments.canadaImplications: Canadian suppliers face origin, technology and product-coverage requirements. Treating market access to Canada and China as interchangeable would miss these constraints.

assessments.name: Agriculture and market access
assessments.summary: Canada remains a large U.S. agricultural market; China exposure is commodity-specific.

questions.title: What is the connection?
questions.text: U.S. agricultural exports serve both markets. The source profile distinguishes Canada’s food-product demand from China’s soybean, livestock-product and feed purchases.

questions.title: Why does it matter to the United States?
questions.text: Farm receipts depend on commodity prices, harvests and market access. A list of products eligible for negotiations is not a shipment or an order.

questions.title: What does the evidence establish?
questions.text: The FAS 2025 profiles record USD28.68 billion exported to Canada and USD8.27 billion to China, with separate commodity values and volumes.

questions.title: What remains uncertain?
questions.text: FAS and ERS publications show different estimates/vintages. Post-September 2026 sales and any displacement of Canadian products require later commodity-level evidence.

assessments.canadaImplications: Canadian producers may face competition, supply-chain opportunities or market diversion. These are exposure channels, not measured gains or losses caused by the framework.

assessments.name: Energy exports and investment
assessments.summary: Canadian crude supplies U.S. refiners; U.S.–China energy flows vary sharply by fuel.

questions.title: What is the connection?
questions.text: The U.S. imports large volumes of Canadian crude while also exporting petroleum products. Its exports to China include different crude, gas and petrochemical channels.

questions.title: Why does it matter to the United States?
questions.text: Refinery configurations, logistics, prices and destination changes matter alongside tariffs. Lower trade value does not necessarily mean lower physical energy supply.

questions.title: What does the evidence establish?
questions.text: EIA provides distinct 2025 crude, petroleum-product and LNG measures. The detailed China LNG series reports 546 million cubic feet, despite near-zero descriptions in rounded narratives.

questions.title: What remains uncertain?
questions.text: Volumes, prices and export destination do not establish net welfare or the effect of a new agreement. Crude barrels and gas cubic feet cannot be added into one physical total.

assessments.canadaImplications: Canadian diversification can change U.S. sourcing exposure. That effect needs measured volumes and completed infrastructure rather than crediting every existing asset to a new MOU.

assessments.name: Financial services
assessments.summary: Market-access commitments and broad services totals answer different questions.

questions.title: What is the connection?
questions.text: USMCA financial-services provisions support covered U.S.–Canada transactions. Phase One includes China-facing financial-services commitments, while separate securities restrictions apply to designated entities.

questions.title: Why does it matter to the United States?
questions.text: Banks, insurers and investors face market-access, supervisory, data and security rules. Sales by overseas affiliates are distinct from cross-border service exports.

questions.title: What does the evidence establish?
questions.text: USTR reports 2025 all-services exports and imports for both partners. These are labelled broad context and are not represented as financial-services-only totals.

questions.title: What remains uncertain?
questions.text: A comparable 2026 bilateral financial-services revenue or employment result is not established here. Treaty commitments do not prove that every licensing or market-access barrier has been removed.

assessments.canadaImplications: Canadian financial firms must distinguish U.S. market access, Chinese opportunities and rules that affect specific technologies or designated securities.

assessments.name: Technology and digital trade
assessments.summary: Digital-trade commitments coexist with targeted export controls and licensing changes.

questions.title: What is the connection?
questions.text: USMCA covers specified digital trade and data issues with Canada. China-facing controls address particular chips, end uses, entities and covered technologies.

questions.title: Why does it matter to the United States?
questions.text: U.S. firms weigh market access and production networks against compliance costs and security requirements. A licensing policy is not equivalent to a shipment prohibition for every product.

questions.title: What does the evidence establish?
questions.text: The timeline includes the 2019 Huawei action, 2022 semiconductor controls, 2025 connected-vehicle rule and January 2026 case-by-case licensing policy for selected chips.

questions.title: What remains uncertain?
questions.text: The review has no comprehensive 2026 digital-only bilateral trade series, and does not count licenses as exports. Technical thresholds and later amendments require the current rule text.

assessments.canadaImplications: Canadian suppliers can be affected by U.S.-origin technology rules and vehicle supply-chain requirements even when their customers or assembly locations are outside the United States.

assessments.name: Defence and security
assessments.summary: Alliance integration, cyber-risk response and counternarcotics cooperation have different mechanisms.

questions.title: What is the connection?
questions.text: NORAD is a longstanding binational U.S.–Canada command. U.S.–China policy combines security restrictions with selective counternarcotics coordination; joint cyber advisories also involve Canada.

questions.title: Why does it matter to the United States?
questions.text: Security measures can constrain commercial choices while cooperation addresses shared threats. Fentanyl precursor controls should not be confused with a finding that all Chinese chemical trade is illicit.

questions.title: What does the evidence establish?
questions.text: Primary sources establish NORAD’s missions, a 2024 U.S.–China working group, precursor-policy developments and a joint critical-infrastructure cyber advisory.

questions.title: What remains uncertain?
questions.text: These records do not establish a new bilateral defence-export total, a net employment effect, or a causal reduction in trafficking and deaths attributable to the working group.

assessments.canadaImplications: Canada has operational and regulatory exposure through continental defence, joint cyber response and cross-border supply chains. An advisory is risk evidence rather than a quantified Canadian commercial loss.

assessments.name: Investment and screening
assessments.summary: Accumulated investment and security review are separate policy channels.

questions.title: What is the connection?
questions.text: BEA measures investment stocks. CFIUS reviews covered inbound transactions; separate U.S. rules address specified outbound investment connected to China.

questions.title: Why does it matter to the United States?
questions.text: The location of a foreign parent, ultimate beneficial owner and operating affiliate can differ. Regulations distinguish particular investors and technologies rather than all capital from a country.

questions.title: What does the evidence establish?
questions.text: BEA country workbooks provide comparable 2020–2025 positions, financial flows and investment income for Canada and China. Treasury separately documents the outbound rules, an enforcement penalty and a 2026 proposal.

questions.title: What remains uncertain?
questions.text: Annual investment positions and flows do not establish completed 2026 factory spending, a causal policy effect or net jobs. Parent-country classification differs from ultimate ownership; proposed expanded rules remain separate from the in-force rule.

assessments.canadaImplications: Canadian excepted-state status is conditional and limited. It does not automatically clear every Canadian investment or turn a U.S. stock value into completed Canadian factory spending.

assessments.name: Agreements and dialogue
assessments.summary: USMCA, Phase One and the 30-for-30 recommendations have different legal and commercial status.

questions.title: What is the connection?
questions.text: USMCA governs covered North American trade. The 2020 Phase One agreement and the 2026 Board of Trade provide China-facing commitments and dialogue, alongside continuing restrictions.

questions.title: Why does it matter to the United States?
questions.text: Commercial planning depends on tariff-line coverage, implementation steps, review procedures and the period measured. Cooperation and restrictive measures can operate at the same time.

questions.title: What does the evidence establish?
questions.text: Official sources distinguish USMCA entry into force, the 2026 non-extension review outcome, specified Canada Section 338 coverage, and recommended U.S.–China product lists.

questions.title: What remains uncertain?
questions.text: The USD30 billion figure is a historical product-scope reference in each direction. Trade data through August 2026 precede the September recommendations and cannot demonstrate their result.

assessments.canadaImplications: Canadian businesses face both U.S. restrictions and potential competition from non-sensitive U.S.–China trade. Net Canadian outcomes remain a separate measurement question.

methods: Coverage is a defined register of official and primary government sources across eight topics, not a claim to contain every policy instrument or all possible statistical series.

The goods series uses U.S. Census values in nominal USD millions and is not seasonally adjusted. U.S. exports include re-exports. Canada’s domestic-export customs series and balance-of-payments indicators use different definitions and currencies.

Annual goods charts include complete years only. The latest incomplete year is shown separately as year-to-date and compared only with the same months of the previous year. Source-reported annual totals can differ slightly from sums of rounded monthly values.

Services estimates come from the linked USTR country summaries. They cover all services, not financial services or digital services alone. Do not combine vintages or infer affiliate sales from cross-border exports.
BEA historical-cost positions are accumulated stocks. Parent-country and ultimate-owner positions are alternative classifications. Neither is completed capex or a net job count.

Policy dates distinguish announcement, publication, legal effectiveness, phased compliance and proposal. A historical tariff milestone is not a complete current landed-rate schedule. Product origin, tariff classification, exclusions and other measures matter.
The 30-for-30 framework’s referenced value is not new spending, a purchase order or an observed export gain. Goods observations through August 2026 predate the September recommendations.
USITC automotive job and revenue figures are model estimates relative to a counterfactual. They are labelled separately from observed shipments and payroll employment.

FAS and ERS agricultural estimates differ in the reviewed publications; this register uses the named FAS profiles for its commodity comparisons and preserves the alternative source as a reconciliation note. Rounded near-zero energy narratives do not replace a small positive detailed series.

No U.S. national, state, province or firm employment total is allocated from aggregate trade values. State-level jobs, net welfare, real value added, completed 2026 investment and causal policy effects are gaps unless a separately identified source establishes them.

Daily collection refreshes Census observations and checks registered source pages. A changed source flags a substantive review; it does not automatically rewrite a reviewed finding or turn a proposed rule into an implemented measure.
Canada implications are analytical inferences from the documented policy and trade channels. They are not estimates of Canadian gains or losses.

researchNotes.title: Revised goods vintage
researchNotes.note: The live Census country tables reconcile with the rounded current USTR goods summaries. Earlier 2025 release vintages can differ; the dashboard does not mix their totals.

researchNotes.title: Agriculture definitions and vintages
researchNotes.note: The FAS country profiles and ERS summary show different agricultural export estimates. Preserve the issuer, vintage and commodity coverage rather than averaging them.

researchNotes.title: Small positive LNG volume
researchNotes.note: Use the detailed annual LNG series (546 million cubic feet in 2025), rather than interpreting a rounded near-zero narrative as literal zero.

researchNotes.title: Framework implementation gap
researchNotes.note: Both governments describe recommendations and domestic legal procedures. A completed reciprocal tariff implementation schedule was not established from these sources in this review.

researchNotes.title: Investment stocks differ from flows
researchNotes.note: The 2025 China-parent U.S. position is USD19,009 million; the net financial transaction flow is minus USD89 million. These are different measures. The country workbooks supply 72 country/year/direction/measure observations, including source cell references.
